data.narrative:
Terrestrial Energy is a public-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $280M to date. The valuation universe comprises 8 comparable peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private companies (Oklo, Nano Nuclear Energy, X-Energy, Fuse Energy, NuScale Power) operating in the nuclear energy sector.

The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy sector. The analysis identified only 2 same-stage peers and zero adjacent-stage peers meeting narrow filtering criteria, falling short of the minimum 3 datapoints required for meaningful triangulation. The broader nuclear energy universe contains 4 same-sector peers, but none satisfy the combined constraints of stage proximity and valuation tier similarity that would make a cross-sector median statistically reliable.

Without sufficient granular peer data, this valuation cannot support a defensible range via traditional comparable-company methods. Meaningful analysis would require either: (1) expansion to adjacent clean-energy or infrastructure sectors with comparable capital intensity and development timelines; (2) direct engagement with recent transaction multiples or financing rounds among the identified private peers; or (3) deployment of DCF-based approaches using disclosed project timelines and capital requirements. The scarcity of mature, profitable nuclear companies in public markets remains the primary constraint on this analysis.
